sections.h2: Where do Northampton County deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds works from Room L116 of the county government center at 669 Washington Street in Easton. Phone 610-829-6210. Staff are at the counter until half past four, but a recording that needs a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m.

The division records, images and stores deeds, mortgages and other real estate papers filed in the county. Each document gets a volume and page reference, then it is imaged and made available for viewing and copying. It also collects the fees and taxes on property transfers and passes them along.

Sellers reach this office at the end of the transaction. The title company gets the deed signed, carries it to Easton, and the recording puts the buyer's name on the public record. Most deeds need a parcel certification, so a courier who shows up at 4:15 may be told to come back tomorrow.

sections.h2: What are the Northampton County recording fees?
sections.html:
Filing a deed runs $76.25 on the schedule that began December 1, 2025. The price assumes four pages and four names at most, with parcel certification added on top.

Northampton County recording fees, effective December 1, 2025
DocumentFee
Parcel certification (each parcel)$10.00
Deed$76.25
Mortgage$76.25
Mortgage satisfaction, assignment or release$61.75
Extra page after the fourth$2.00
Extra name after the fourth$0.50
Installment sales agreement$59.75
Notary bond and commission$38.50

Source: the Recorder of Deeds fee schedule published on the county website. An easement or right of way costs $59.75, and a power of attorney used to sell real estate costs $18.50 plus parcel certification.

Smaller lines round out the schedule. A Statement of Value costs $2 and counts toward the page total, certifications cost $2.50, and copies are fifty cents a page.

sections.h2: How should a closing agent pay the Northampton County recorder?
sections.html:
Make payment out to "Recorder of Deeds." Personal checks are refused. Business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash all work, and a single check can cover five documents at most.

The exact amount has to accompany each document, and the office turns away overpayments. Closing packages built on a rough guess run into that rule, so build the number line by line from the schedule above.

  • Count the pages first, then add the $2 for every page past four.
  • Add $10 for each parcel on documents marked with an asterisk on the schedule.
  • Count names past four at $0.50 each.
  • Add the separate transfer tax payment if the deed is taxable.

sections.h2: Which paper rules does the Easton recorder enforce?
sections.html:
The schedule opens with its house rules, and they decide whether a deed is recorded or returned.

  • Parcel numbers must appear on every document that relates to real estate. The county points filers to its public parcel search at ncpub.org.
  • Pages are meant to be letter size, 8.5 by 11 inches. A paper that cannot comply, with 8.5 by 14 as the only allowed exception, pays a $10 penalty.
  • Blanket assignments, releases and satisfaction pieces are refused.
  • Anything coming back by mail needs a return envelope with the right postage already on it.

Not every filing is a deed. If a sale involves a new lot line or survey, the county charges $35 for the first page of a subdivision, site or survey plan and $30 for each added page. State highway plans cost $15 for the first page and $3 after that, and a lease for 30 years or longer costs $59.75. Full-size map copies up to 36 by 48 inches are $25.

The county also states that every document is microfilmed and open to public inspection, so what gets filed in Easton becomes searchable by anyone. The page count matters because the fee is built on it. A deed with a long legal description and an attached exhibit can pass four pages quickly, so check before you assume the base price.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a Northampton County sale?
sections.html:
On a taxable deed the recorder takes the state's 1 percent along with whatever local transfer tax the municipality and school district impose. State rules hold the grantor and the grantee jointly responsible.

The state exempts some deeds, among them certain family transfers, deeds to a government body and inherited property. If you believe your deed fits, tell the title agent early. For the local share, call the recorder's office and give the municipality where the house stands, because the figure can differ from one borough or township to the next.

Who actually pays is a matter for the sales contract, so read that clause before closing.

sections.h2: What is the Northampton County housing picture for sellers?
sections.html:
Easton is the seat and Bethlehem the biggest city of this Lehigh Valley county. Carved from Bucks County in 1752, it spans 377 square miles, with the Delaware River along its eastern edge and the Lehigh River cutting through.

Heavy industry shaped it. Bethlehem Steel was based in Bethlehem until it was dissolved in 2003, and the region also made cement. The Census Bureau estimated 324,411 residents in 2025.

Housing costs sit well below Montgomery County to the south. The latest five-year survey shows a $308,600 median home, $89,184 median household income and owners in 71.1 percent of occupied units. The county adopted a home rule charter in 1978, with a county executive and a council.

sections.h2: Which Northampton County municipalities send deeds to this office?
sections.html:
All of them. Two cities, Bethlehem and Easton, sit among many boroughs and townships, yet every deed for land inside the county line is recorded in the same Easton office.

The largest places by the 2010 census were Bethlehem at 74,982 people, a city that spills partly into Lehigh County, then Easton at 26,800, Bethlehem Township at 23,730, Palmer Township at 20,691 and Forks Township at 14,721. Smaller boroughs include Northampton, Wilson, Hellertown, Nazareth, Bangor, Pen Argyl and Wind Gap.

Two points follow for a seller. Part of Bethlehem lies in Lehigh County, a different county with its own recorder, so confirm which side your house is on before planning the closing. And local transfer tax and school district bills follow the municipality, so a sale in Hellertown can price out differently from one in Palmer Township.

sections.h2: What should I check before closing a Northampton County sale?
sections.html:
Most delays are paper problems, not legal ones. Work through the list a few days ahead.

  • Confirm the parcel number on the deed matches the county's parcel search.
  • Count pages and names to get the exact fee, with no overpayment.
  • Ask whether the title company will deliver by 4:00 p.m., since parcel-certified recordings close early.
  • Pull the tax certification and any unpaid tax before the closing date.
  • Ask the title agent how the Statement of Value is being counted in the page total.
  • Collect a return envelope with correct postage if the deed is coming back by mail.

Open mortgage balances get released through a satisfaction piece, which costs $61.75 to record. Ask the lender how long it takes to file one so the buyer's title is clean.

faqs.q: What will it run me to file a deed in Easton?
faqs.a: Plan on $76.25 for a deed of four pages and four names. Add $10 per certified parcel, $2 for each extra page and 50 cents for each extra name.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Northampton County recorder with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. The county takes business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash, and caps a check at five documents.

faqs.q: Can I overpay the recording fee in Northampton County?
faqs.a: No. The office wants the exact fee with each document and refuses overpayments, so work out the total before the package goes out.

faqs.q: When does the Northampton County recorder stop taking documents?
faqs.a: The counter stays open until 4:30 p.m., but anything needing a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m. A later deed waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Northampton County sale?
faqs.a: State law makes both sides jointly responsible for the 1 percent state tax. The contract decides who actually pays, so check that clause.
